source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Judge{H1777} not, lest{H6435} you be judged{H1777}.

one_way_hebrew: אל תדינו פן תדונו — a four-word chiasm on the root דין (H1777), the rabbinic verb of judging: m. Avot 2:4, אל תדין את חברך עד שתגיע למקומו ('judge not thy fellow until thou come into his place') uses the same verb in the same maxim-form. Greek κρίνω renders it, but only the Hebrew shows the saying wearing the Mishnah's own dress.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ו (Perek 26) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (7:1): תדינו] תדונו DG.

verses.translation: With whatever{H335} judgment{H1779} you judge{H1777}, and with whatever measure{H4060} you measure{H4058}, it will be measured{H4058} to you.

one_way_hebrew: The measure-for-measure formula is the Mishnah's own: במדה שאדם מודד בה מודדין לו — 'with the measure a man measures, they measure to him' (m. Sotah 1:7) — built on מדה/מדד (H4060/H4058) exactly as here. Greek ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται translates the Hebrew maxim that was already proverbial in the land.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:2): ימודד] ימודו ABCDEFG; ובאיזה] באיזה E; B omits a clause by haplography.

verses.translation: And why{H4100} do you see{H7200} the straw{H7179} in the eye{H5869} of your fellow{H2108}, but do not see{H7200} the beam{H6982} that is in your own eyes{H5869}?

one_way_hebrew: קש (H7179) — the dry stubble of Exod 5:12 and Isa 5:24; קורה (H6982) — the roof-beam of 2 Kgs 6:2,5 and Song 1:17. The joke stands on two native building-and-harvest words; Greek κάρφος and δοκός translate them.
translation_notes: זולתך — literally 'the one besides you' (זולת, H2108), the text's regular word for the other person; mss at v. 4 substitute לרעך ('your neighbor').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:3): תראו] תראה BEF; קורה] קודם C.

verses.translation: And how{H349} do you say{H559} to your fellow{H2108}: Wait{H3803} for me a little{H2191}, and I will cast out{H3318} the straw{H7179} from your eyes{H5869} — and behold{H2009}, the beam{H6982} is in your own eyes?

one_way_hebrew: כתר לי זעיר — Job 36:2 verbatim: כתר לי זעיר ואחוך ('Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee'), Elihu's preface to setting another man straight. The two rare words — כתר 'wait' (H3803) and זעיר 'a little' (H2191) — stand side by side only there in Scripture. Greek Matthew has a bare ἄφες ('let me'); no back-translator from that Greek lands on Job's exact idiom, but a Hebrew author reaching for 'give me a moment while I correct you' quotes the Bible's one professional corrector.
translation_notes: הקרה — the printed text spells הקורה ('the beam') defectively here; the full spelling stands in v. 5.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:4): לזולתך] לרעך EF; הנה] והנה ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Hypocrite{H2611}! Cast out{H3318} first{H6924} the beam{H6982} from your own eyes{H5869}, and afterward cast out the straw{H7179} from the eye of your fellow{H2108}.

one_way_hebrew: החנף — again the native חנף (H2611) where Greek transliterates the theater-word ὑποκριτά; see 6:2, where the text itself glosses חנפים with the foreign 'ipocrates.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:5): תוציא¹] הוצא AD, הוציא EFG; מעיניך] שבעיניך DEFG; ואח״כ] ואחר DEFG.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: Do not give{H5414} holy{H6944} flesh{H1320} to dogs{H3611}, and do not set{H7760} your pearls{H6443} before{H6440} swine{H2386}, lest{H6435} they chew{H3765} them before your eyes{H5869} and turn to tear{H7167} you.

one_way_hebrew: בשר קדש — 'holy flesh,' the Temple term for sacrificial meat (Hag 2:12; Jer 11:15), where Greek has the abstract τὸ ἅγιον ('that which is holy'). Torah law is the backdrop: torn flesh goes to the dogs (Exod 22:30), holy flesh never does — the Hebrew states a priestly rule, not a metaphor alone.

יכרסמנו (H3765, kirsem) — a verb that occurs exactly once in Scripture: Ps 80:14, יכרסמנה חזיר מיער ('the boar out of the wood doth ravage it'). Swine and כרסם meet only in that psalm and here; the saying is built on the psalm's boar. Greek καταπατήσουσιν ('trample') shows no trace of it.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew adds 'before your eyes' (לעיניכם) — you watch the desecration; Greek has 'trample them under their feet' (ms C reads ברגלהם, 'with their feet,' assimilating toward the Greek).
translation_notes: The printed base text reads פניכם ('your face'); mss AEF read פניניכם and BDGH פנינכם — 'your PEARLS' (פנינים, H6443, the pearls of Prov 3:15) — which the sense requires and Howard's English follows ('your (pearls)'). The base reading lost a syllable (פני[ני]כם); the words array keeps the printed form with the pearls sense.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ז (Perek 27) begins here.
The circulating transcription omitted קדש; the scan of Howard's text reads בשר קדש — restored here.
Howard's apparatus (7:6): להם] + ישו A; קדש] קודש BD; פניכם] פניניכם AEF, פנינכם BDGH; יכרסמנו] יכרסמנה ADGH; חזיר] החזירים A, חזירים H; לעיניכם] לעינכם A, ברגלהם C; אותה²] omit ADEFG.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads differently: 'do not speak about the holy writings before the refusing animals, and do not bring the precious words before the pigs.'

verses.translation: Ask{H7592} from El{H410} and it will be given{H5414} to you; seek{H1245} and you will find{H4672}; knock{H1849} and it will be opened{H6605} to you.

one_way_hebrew: דפקו (H1849) — the knock of Song 5:2, קול דודי דופק ('the voice of my beloved that knocketh'), the one knocking at a door in all of Scripture — the beloved at the door of the loved. Greek κρούετε is generic.
The Hebrew names the addressee: 'ask FROM EL' (שאלו מהאל) — absent from the Greek's bare 'ask, and it shall be given you.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:7): וינתן] ויתן A.

verses.translation: Everyone who asks{H7592} will receive{H6901}; and for the one who seeks{H1245}, it will be found{H4672}; and to the one who calls{H7121}, it will be opened{H6605}.
words: and to the one who calls

greek_deviations: 'To the one who CALLS (ולקורא) it will be opened' — Greek repeats 'to him that knocketh.' The Hebrew answers the door-knock of v. 7 with קרא, the covenant verb of calling on God: 'YHWH is nigh unto all them that call upon him' (Ps 145:18). The door opens to the caller — prayer, not knuckles.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:8): יקבל] יקבלו G; ולקורא] ולקרוא B.

verses.translation: Who{H4310} among you, whose son{H1121} asks{H1245} him to break{H6536} bread{H3899}, will give{H5414} him a stone{H68}?

one_way_hebrew: לפרוס לחם — 'to break bread': Isa 58:7 (פרס לרעב לחמך, 'deal thy bread to the hungry') and Lam 4:4, where 'the young children ask bread, and no man breaketh it unto them' — the exact scene of a child asking for the breaking of bread. Greek ('whom his son shall ask for a loaf') has no breaking; the Hebrew idiom carries Lamentations' ache inside the question.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:9): לפרוס] + לו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Or if he asks{H1245} for a fish{H1709}, will he give{H5414} him a serpent{H5175}?

textual_notes: The circulating transcription read אמ and לחש; the scan of Howard's text reads אם and נחש ('serpent') — corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (7:10): ויתן] + לו A.

verses.translation: And if you{H859}, being{H1961} evil{H7451}, come{H935} to set good{H2896} gifts{H4979} before yourselves{H6440}, how much more will your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064} give{H5414} his good{H2896} spirit{H7307} to those who seek him{H1245}?

one_way_hebrew: רוחו הטוב — 'his GOOD SPIRIT': the phrase of Neh 9:20, ורוחך הטובה נתת להשכילם ('thou gavest also thy good spirit to instruct them'), and Ps 143:10 (רוחך טובה). The Father's gift is named in Scripture's own words for the Spirit given to teach.
למבקשיו — 'to those who SEEK him,' the verb of vv. 7-8 (בקשו... יבקש) closing the chain: ask, seek, find, receive — one Hebrew root carries the promise through.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew reads 'give GOOD THINGS to them that ask him'; Luke 11:13 reads 'give the HOLY SPIRIT to them that ask him.' The Shem Tov Hebrew stands with Luke — the gift is the Spirit — and names it with Nehemiah's idiom, 'his good spirit.'
The base text's first clause reads 'to set good gifts BEFORE YOURSELVES (לפניכם)'; mss A and BDEFG read לבניכם/לבנכם ('to your children'), as in the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:11): תבואו] תבאו AEF, תביאו DG; לפניכם] לבניכם A, לבנכם BDEFG; הטוב] הטובה ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And everything{H3605} that you wish{H7521} that the sons{H1121} of man{H120} should do{H6213} for you, do{H6213} for them: this{H2063} is the Torah{H8451} and the words{H1697} of the prophets{H5030}.

one_way_hebrew: זאת התורה — 'this is the Torah': the Pentateuch's own recurring heading (Num 19:14 זאת התורה; Deut 4:44 וזאת התורה). The golden rule is sealed with the formula the Torah uses to introduce its statutes — in Hebrew the sentence sounds like a citation from Sinai; Greek 'this is the law and the prophets' translates the words but not the echo.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:12): ודברי] וספרי EF ('and the books of the prophets').

verses.translation: At that time{H2165} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Enter{H935} by the narrow{H6862} gate{H8179}, for the gate of Abaddon{H11} is wide{H7342} and deep{H4688}, and many{H7227} walk{H1980} in it.

one_way_hebrew: שער האבדון — 'the gate of ABADDON': אבדון (H11) is Scripture's name for the realm of destruction, Sheol's twin (Prov 15:11 שאול ואבדון; Job 26:6). And מצולה (H4688) is the drowning deep — Jonah's מצולה (Jonah 2:4) and the psalmist's ('I sink in deep mire... I am come into deep waters,' Ps 69:3). The Hebrew's wide gate is the mouth of the Pit, broad and DEEP; Greek ἀπώλεια ('destruction') is abstract, and the depth is absent from the Greek altogether.
translation_notes: לתלמידו — printed singular ('to his disciple'); read with all translators as לתלמידיו ('to his disciples'), the yod of the plural suffix dropped in the ms.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ח (Perek 28) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (7:13): באו] בואו G; הצר] הזה EF; ומצולה] ומסילה A, מצלה DEFG; ורבים] והבית EF.

verses.translation: How narrow{H6862} is the gate{H8179}, and heavy{H3515} the way{H1870} that leads straight{H3474} to life{H2416} — and few{H4592} are those who find{H4672} it!

one_way_hebrew: The two verses map Proverbs' geography: 'The way of life is upward to the wise, that he may depart from Sheol beneath' (Prov 15:24) — the straight way to life above (v. 14), the deep gate of Abaddon below (v. 13; Prov 15:11 names שאול ואבדון thirteen verses earlier in the same chapter). The Hebrew discourse walks inside Prov 15; the Greek's 'destruction... life' keeps the doctrine but loses the address.
greek_deviations: 'HEAVY (כבד) the way' — Greek τεθλιμμένη ('compressed, afflicted'). The Hebrew way to life weighs; it is not merely cramped.
translation_notes: המשייר — printed with transposed letters for המיישר ('that leads straight,' from ישר, H3474; so mss BDEF המיישר, AG המישר); Howard renders '(that leads straight).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:14): המשייר] המישר AG, המיישר BDEF; וכבד] וכמה כבד ABDEFG; השער צר] transposed in ABDEFG; אותה] אותו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: Beware{H2094} of the prophets{H5030} of falsehood{H8267} who come{H935} to you in garments{H4403} of wool{H6785}, resembling{H1819} sheep{H6629}, but within{H8432} they are tearing{H2963} wolves{H2061}.

one_way_hebrew: נביאי השקר — Jeremiah's construct again (Jer 23:26; cf. 24:11,24 on this site); and זאבים טורפים is Ezekiel's charge against the leaders: 'her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey' (כזאבים טרפי טרף, Ezek 22:27; cf. Gen 49:27 זאב יטרף). Prophets of the lie outside, Ezekiel's wolves inside — both halves in the prophets' own words.

במלבושי צמר — 'garments of WOOL,' the sheep's own fiber and the prophet's professional costume: Zech 13:4, the false prophets 'shall not wear a hairy mantle to deceive.' Greek 'sheep's clothing' (ἐνδύμασιν προβάτων) keeps the picture, loses the wardrobe.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ט (Perek 29) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (7:15): צמר] הצמר ABDEFG; שמתוכם] שבתוכם ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And by their deeds{H4639} you will recognize{H5234} them. Does a man{H120} gather{H3950} grapes{H6025} from the thorns{H6975}, or figs{H8384} from the briers{H1303}?

one_way_hebrew: ברקונים (H1303, barqanim) — Gideon's threshing-briers (Judg 8:7,16), a word found nowhere else in Scripture; Greek τρίβολοι ('thistles') is generic. With קוצים (Gen 3:18's curse-thorns), the Hebrew asks its question with Scripture's two sharpest words.
greek_deviations: 'By their DEEDS (מעשיהם) you will recognize them' — Greek reads 'by their fruits.' The Hebrew gives the decoded sense here and lets v. 20 hold metaphor and decoding together (see there).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:16): מן] בין G.

verses.translation: For every{H3605} good{H2896} tree{H6086} makes{H6213} good fruit{H6529}, and every bad{H7451} tree makes bad fruit.

one_way_hebrew: עשה פרי — 'MAKE fruit': Gen 1:11-12's own grammar (עץ פרי עשה פרי, 'the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind'). In Greek ποιεῖν καρπόν is a borrowed Hebraism; in Hebrew it is the syntax of creation — each tree does what it was made to do.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:17): פרי רע] omit D.

verses.translation: The good{H2896} tree{H6086} cannot{H3201} make{H6213} bad{H7451} fruit{H6529}, and a bad tree cannot make good fruit.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:18): רע¹] הרע G; ועץ²] והעץ EF; C omits the first clause by haplography.

verses.translation: And every tree{H6086} that does not make{H6213} good{H2896} fruit{H6529} is burned{H8313}.

greek_deviations: No 'hewn down': Greek adds ἐκκόπτεται ('is cut down and cast into fire'); the Hebrew has only the burning.
translation_notes: The base text reads כאשר ישרף (awkward, 'as/when it is burned'); mss BDEFG read באש ישרף ('is burned IN THE FIRE'), A drops כאשר. The באש reading is surely right, כאשר a copyist's slip; Howard renders '(is burned in the fire).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:19): כאשר] omit A, באש BDEFG; ישרף] ישרוף BD.

verses.translation: Therefore{H3651}, according to their fruits{H6529} — that is to say, by their deeds{H4639} — you will recognize{H5234} them.

greek_deviations: The verse carries its own interpretive gloss: כפריים ר״ל במעשיהם — 'by their fruits, that is to say (ר״ל = רוצה לומר), by their deeds.' Metaphor and decoding stand side by side inside the Hebrew text, the same annotating habit as the לעז glosses (6:2, 24:14); Greek Matthew has only the metaphor. The symbol is explained, not dissolved: fruit MEANS deeds.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:20): כפריים] בפרים ינכרום A.

verses.translation: For everyone who says{H559} to me{H413}: My lord{H113}! — will not come{H935} into the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}; but he who does{H6213} the will{H7522} of my Father{H1} who is in heaven will enter{H3664} the kingdom of heaven.

one_way_hebrew: העושה רצון אבי — 'the doer of my Father's WILL (רצון)': the rabbinic category עושה רצונו — 'those who do His will' (m. Avot 5:20's בנים למקום idiom-family) — the standing Hebrew name for the obedient. Greek ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα translates the phrase the synagogue already used.
greek_deviations: Single address — אדוני, 'my lord' — where Greek doubles κύριε κύριε; the doubled cry is kept for the day of judgment in v. 22. And the Hebrew uses two verbs of entry (לא יבא... יכנס) where the Greek has one.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:21): האומר] אומר G; B omits אבל... שמים by haplography; שמים²] omit A.

verses.translation: Many{H7227} will say{H559} to me in that day{H3117}: My lord{H113}, my lord{H113}! Did we not prophesy{H5012} in your name{H8034}, and in your name cast out{H3318} demons{H7700}, and do{H6213} many{H7227} signs{H226} upon your name?

one_way_hebrew: שדים (H7700) — Scripture's own demon-word: 'they sacrificed unto shedim, not to God' (Deut 32:17; Ps 106:37); Greek δαιμόνια translates it. And the claim hammers the Name three times — בשמך... ובשמך... על שמך — the credential of Deut 13:2-3's false prophet, whose sign succeeds and whose direction is still rejected: the law behind 24:24 governs here too.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:22): אומרים] יאמרו ABDEFG; אלי] לי EF; נבאנו] נבחרו EF; שדים] omit C; הוצאתנו] הוצאנו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And then{H227} I will say{H559} to them: I never{H5769} knew{H3045} you. Depart{H5493} from me, all{H3605} you workers{H6466} of iniquity{H205}.

one_way_hebrew: סורו ממני כל פועלי און — Ps 6:9 letter for letter: סורו ממני כל פעלי און ('Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity'). The Hebrew text QUOTES David; Greek Matthew translates him (ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν). In the psalm the speaker is the weeping man whose prayer YHWH has heard (Ps 6:9b) — the very standing the name-sayers of v. 22 claimed and lacked. Only the Hebrew shows the sentence as a citation with its context loaded.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:23): אמר] אומר ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: Everyone who hears{H8085} these{H428} words{H1697} and does{H6213} them is like{H1819} a wise{H2450} man{H376} who built{H1129} a house{H1004} on the rock{H5553}.

one_way_hebrew: The pair חכם (here) / שוטה (v. 26) — wise man and shoteh — is the Mishnah's standing opposition, not the Bible's חכם/כסיל: the parable is told in the living Hebrew of the study-house. Greek φρόνιμος/μωρός translates the pair without its register.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק שלשים (Perek 30) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (7:24): בית] ביתו ABCDEFGH.

verses.translation: And the rain{H1653} came down{H3381} upon it, and the winds{H7307} beat{H5368} it, and it did not fall{H5307}, because its foundation{H3247} was stone{H68}.

one_way_hebrew: 'Because its foundation was STONE (אבן)' — Isa 28:16: 'Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a STONE... a sure foundation (מוסד מוסד); he that believeth shall not make haste.' The Hebrew names Isaiah's אבן; Greek 'founded upon the rock (πέτραν)' keeps the doctrine and loses the oracle. Cf. Prov 10:25: 'the righteous is an everlasting foundation (יסוד עולם).'
translation_notes: מקישות — hiphil of נקש, 'strike, knock' (cf. the Aramaic of Dan 5:6, knees knocking); late Hebrew for the winds' battering.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:25): אותו] בו AH.

verses.translation: And everyone who hears{H8085} these{H428} words{H1697} and does not do{H6213} them is like{H1819} a foolish man{H376} who built{H1129} his house{H1004} on the sand{H2344}.

translation_notes: שוטה — the rabbinic word for a fool (no biblical Strong's); Scripture's אויל and כסיל are passed over for the Mishnah's own term, the natural partner of v. 24's חכם.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:26): יעשם] יעשה EF.

verses.translation: And the rains{H1653} came down{H3381}, and the floods{H2230} came{H935}, and they made it fall{H5307} — falling{H5307} a great{H1419} fall{H4654}.

one_way_hebrew: זרם (H2230) — Isaiah's flood-word: 'as a tempest of hail, a destroying storm, as a flood (זרם) of mighty waters overflowing' (Isa 28:2) — and Isa 28 holds BOTH halves of this parable: the foundation stone laid in Zion (28:16, v. 25's note) and the overflowing flood that sweeps away the refuge of lies (28:17). The two houses are Isa 28's two builders.

נופל מפלה גדולה — the cognate accusative ('falling a great fall'), native Hebrew grammar with מפלה (H4654), Isaiah's ruin-word (Isa 17:1; 23:13); the Greek's 'and great was the fall of it' imitates the Hebrew construction.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:27): ויבואו] ויבאו ACDEFG; H omits ויבואו זרמים; נופל] ונפל H.

verses.translation: And while Yeshua{H3442} was speaking{H1696} these{H428} words{H1697}, all{H3605} the people{H5971} were astonished{H8539} at the abundance{H7230} of the goodness{H2896} of his conduct,

greek_deviations: The crowd marvels 'at the abundance of the goodness of his CONDUCT (הנהגתו)' — Greek reads 'at his TEACHING (διδαχῇ).' In the Hebrew, what stuns them is the man's bearing; his expounding is given its own clause in v. 29. The Greek folds both into doctrine.
translation_notes: הנהגה — the medieval Hebrew word for conduct, comportment; no biblical Strong's.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (7:28): מרוב] מגודל ABCDEFGH; שישו היה מדבר] שהיה מדבר ישו EF; כל העם היו] omit C.

verses.translation: because he was expounding{H1875} to them with great{H1419} power{H3581}, and not as the rest{H7605} of the sages{H2450}.

one_way_hebrew: דורש (H1875) — he 'darshans' to them: the rabbinic verb of expounding Scripture (as at 24:14), the word behind midrash. The scene is a beit-midrash scene: one darshan among the sages, but with power. Greek 'he taught them as one having authority' flattens the setting.
greek_deviations: 'Not as the rest of the SAGES (החכמים)' — Greek reads 'not as their SCRIBES (γραμματεῖς).' The Hebrew counts him among the chakhamim and marks what set him apart; the Greek redraws the line between him and a copyist class.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription read כאשר; the scan of Howard's text reads כשאר ('as the rest of') — corrected here.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 7 in the Shem Tov Hebrew closes the discourse with its scriptural seams showing. (1) 7:23 quotes Ps 6:9 letter for letter — סורו ממני כל פועלי און ('depart from me, all workers of iniquity'); the Greek translates the psalm, the Hebrew IS the psalm. (2) 7:4 opens with Job 36:2's rare two-word idiom כתר לי זעיר ('suffer me a little'), Elihu's preface to correcting a man — unreachable from the Greek's bare 'let me.' (3) 7:6 reads 'HOLY FLESH' (בשר קדש, Hag 2:12 — sacrificial meat, never for dogs, Exod 22:30) and its swine 'CHEW' (יכרסמנו) with a verb found once in Scripture: Ps 80:14's boar. (4) 7:11: the Father gives 'HIS GOOD SPIRIT' (Neh 9:20) 'to those who seek him' — with Luke 11:13 (Holy Spirit) against Greek Matthew's 'good things.' (5) 7:13-14: the wide gate is 'the gate of ABADDON... wide and DEEP (מצולה)' against 'the way that leads straight to LIFE' — Prov 15's own map (15:11 שאול ואבדון, 15:24 the way of life upward, away from Sheol beneath). (6) 7:1-2 are the Mishnah's maxims in the Mishnah's words (אל תדינו on דין as m. Avot 2:4; measure-for-measure as m. Sotah 1:7). (7) 7:20 glosses itself — 'by their fruits, THAT IS TO SAY (ר״ל), by their deeds' — an in-text decoding like the לעז glosses. (8) 7:28-29: the people are astonished at his CONDUCT (הנהגתו), and he expounds (דורש, the midrash-verb) with great power 'not as the rest of the SAGES (החכמים)' — where Greek has 'teaching... not as their scribes.' (9) 7:12 seals the golden rule with the Torah's own heading formula, זאת התורה (Num 19:14). (10) Isa 28 stands under both houses of the closing parable: the foundation stone (28:16, v. 25 יסודו אבן) and the sweeping flood (28:2,17, v. 27 זרמים). Corrections from the scan: 7:6 בשר קדש (transcription dropped קדש), 7:10 נחש for לחש, 7:29 כשאר for כאשר. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 26), 6 (27), 13 (28), 15 (29), and 24 (30).
